author: DTrim99
body:
Yes — Tables A and B are a bracketed form of a formula, and PolicyEngine implements it: property taxes capped at $1,460, minus 8.785% of household income above $8,060 (Table A), times 80% (Table B). Fed your household income of $15,826 that gives (1,460 − 0.08785 × (15,826 − 8,060)) × 0.80 = **$622**, matching your $620 (the $2 is the bracketed tables vs. the continuous formula). So the tables aren't where we differ.

The difference is **household income**. Your Schedule H line 12c is $15,826 — wages only; the $3,885 of interest isn't in it. PolicyEngine includes the interest (household income ≈ $19,211 after the $500 dependent reduction), which gives **$384**.

And I think the interest belongs there: Schedule H counts taxable interest through Wisconsin income (line 7) and nontaxable US-government/municipal interest through the line 9g add-back. On this return the $3,885 isn't in federal AGI (Form 1 line 1 = 15,826), so it's being treated as tax-exempt — in which case line 9g should add it back, but it's blank. With it included the credit is $384. Does that match your reading of line 9g, or is there a reason it stays out?
